newsitem.title: USA: Va. Power North Anna 1 nuke trips off line.
newsitem.headline: Va. Power North Anna 1 nuke trips off line.

text.p: Virginia Power Co's North Anna 1 nuclear power plant, rated at 911 megawatts (MW), tripped off line and is being kept of hot standby, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said Thursday.
The North Anna facility's other nuclear plant, the 909 MW unit 2, was shut Monday for repairs and was expected to come back into service late Thursday, the company said earlier this week.
The event occurred at about 0319 EDT today when North Anna 1 was operating at 100 percent power, according to a report submitted today by Virginia Power to the NRC.
The plant tripped off line after its generator output breaker opened due to 'generator negative phase sequence," the company told the agency.
The North Anna complex in Mineral, Va., is jointly owned by Virginia Power (88.4 percent) and Old Dominion Electric Co-operative (11.6 percent).
Virginia Power's interest in North Anna represents just below 12 percent of its installed generation capacity and about 17 percent of its annual electricity deliveries.
Virginia Power is a subsidiary of Dominion Resources.
